title: The settling sum of the plastic number: sum_{n >= 1} ||rho^n||^2 = rho. The squared distances from the powers of the plastic number to the nearest integers sum to the plastic number itself; the even-power trace of its two hidden conjugates is rho; with the general cubic complex-pair form
abstract: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six statements. Write ||x|| = |x - round x| for the distance from a real number to the nearest integer, and let rho be the plastic number, the real root of x^3 = x + 1 and the smallest Pisot number (Siegel 1944). Convergence of sum_{n >= 1} ||theta^n||^2 for a Pisot number theta is elementary, and Pisot (1938) proved the converse; neither gives the value. (1) For every real rho with rho^3 = rho + 1, sum_{n >= 1} ||rho^n||^2 = rho (as a HasSum). (2) The tsum form of (1). (3) For every complex alpha != rho with alpha^3 = alpha + 1 (one of the two conjugates inside the unit disc), sum_{n >= 0} (alpha^(2n) + conj(alpha)^(2n)) = rho: the even-power trace of the hidden pair is the generator, the mechanism behind (1), because x^3 - x - 1 = (x - 1) x (x + 1) - 1 makes the resolvent trace sum_{roots} 1/(1 - r^2) vanish. (4) For a real theta, a complex alpha with ||alpha|| < 1, and integers a, b, c that are the elementary symmetric functions of (theta, alpha, conj alpha): sum_{n >= 1} (S_n - theta^n)^2 = Re(geo alpha), where S_n are the Newton power sums of x^3 - a x^2 + b x - c and geo alpha = alpha^2/(1 - alpha^2) + conj(alpha)^2/(1 - conj(alpha)^2) + 2 alpha conj(alpha)/(1 - alpha conj(alpha)). (5) Under the same hypotheses, for every N with ||alpha||^N < 1/4, sum_{n >= 1} ||theta^n||^2 = Re(geo alpha) + sum_{n = 1}^{N} (||theta^n||^2 - (S_n - theta^n)^2): Pisot's convergence in quantitative form for the cubic complex-pair case; (1) is the case a = 0, b = -1, c = 1, N = 10 (the smallest N with rho^(-N/2) < 1/4; the n = 10 correction term is zero), with Re(geo alpha) = 2 rho^2 + 3 rho - 2 and correction 2 - 2 rho - 2 rho^2. (6) x^3 = x + 1 has exactly one real solution. Statements 4-5 assume neither theta > 1 nor irreducibility. Pisot's theorem itself is not formalized. Not compared, proved in the repository's library only: the threshold from which the Perrin numbers are the nearest integers to rho^n (n >= 10, sharp at n = 9), a claim previously stated without proof at OEIS A001608 (R. Stephan, 2002); it was a compared statement in the withdrawn submissions of 2026-11-03/04 and was removed from the compared set on 2026-11-05 so that every compared result is one first presented here. Application to time (no compared statement asserts it): in the arithmetic of time the tick is multiplication by rho on Q(rho) and the record is the integer lattice; statement 1 says the total squared distance by which the tick history falls short of its record is exactly one tick's unit, rho, and statement 3 says that unit is returned by the two conjugates that are not seen; the quartic companion Q, Q^4 = Q + 1, is not Pisot, so by Pisot's theorem its series diverges (not proved here). That physical time is this arithmetic is the identification stated in the companion entry PALOMAR-2026-08-19-000006 (the arithmetic of time), as an identification; the theorems here are its arithmetic content. That entry's README Scope section is reproduced verbatim in this entry's README.
